shared_assumptions.atomic_transitions: Lease and rate transitions are serialized. A Rust implementation must establish the corresponding lock, actor or atomic-operation discipline.
shared_assumptions.internal_callback_tokens: Completion tokens originate in the internal reservation lifecycle. The model does not expose a completion API to unauthenticated network senders.
shared_assumptions.nonwrapping_generations: Count generations are mathematical naturals. A finite machine identifier needs a no-wrap or generation-collision argument.
shared_assumptions.complete_event_refinement: Every relevant implementation event and error path is represented by the modeled transition.
shared_assumptions.trusted_clock: Only the trusted monotonic clock issues ticks. One modeled tick has a specified real duration and is never replayed or fabricated by peer traffic.
shared_assumptions.cost_dominance: Each supplied weight bounds real per-entry, per-start or per-processed-policy-operation cost in a common unit, including the allocated state charged to that component. A policy-operation weight covers denied attempts and stale publications as well as successful operations; input and roster bounds must justify it.
shared_assumptions.fifo_projection: The waiting rank correctly projects a critical FIFO queue; later critical work is enqueued behind the fixed target request.
shared_assumptions.scheduled_rounds: A completed modeled round really services one critical request. The runtime must execute enough such rounds to establish a wall-clock bound.
shared_assumptions.executor_wakeup: The executor honors the modeled wakeup request and eventually gives a pending poll another turn.
shared_assumptions.authenticated_membership: The verified flag includes full signature checking and authenticated binding of the record to its committee identity and presented epoch.
shared_assumptions.stable_committee_index: Each current committee member has one stable, unique slot. Record senders cannot choose another member slot or create new roster slots.
shared_assumptions.atomic_policy_publication: Each complete policy view is immutable; generation comparison and publication are atomic. Receipt validation and the resulting authorization linearize with publication, or retain equivalent protection through use.
shared_assumptions.policy_input_validation: Health, epoch, membership mappings, roster and the positive recovery threshold come from validated authoritative inputs. Snapshot generation orders local publication, not external governance versions. Input freshness and epoch ordering require separate validation.
shared_assumptions.policy_receipt_provenance: PolicyReceipt values are internal results of policy queries for the actual authenticated peer. Untrusted input cannot construct or alter a receipt, its identity or its allowed flag.
shared_assumptions.stable_resource_configuration: Bucket capacity and pending-pool capacity are fixed during each modeled run. Restarts and runtime resource-cap changes require additional transitions and proofs.
shared_assumptions.canonical_source_keys: Each Count key represents one canonical validated source or prefix under a fixed normalization policy. PeerIds cannot choose or reset this binding. The initial runtime table has unique canonical keys.
shared_assumptions.source_restriction_classification: SourceClear means no unexpired rate debt or ban. The supplied restriction preserves all security-relevant state, including simultaneous debt and bans. Module 27 models churn, module 28 restriction events, and module 29 their keyed composition. Module 37 couples source charging to shared credits and pending ownership. Runtime lookup, atomic enforcement, complete classification and policy/resource integration still require refinement.
shared_assumptions.fixed_source_quota: The per-source quota is fixed during each restriction or composed source-system trace and counts admitted operations since trusted debt expiry. Initial debt is within that quota; composed traces require a bound for every initial resident. Mathematical Count arithmetic requires checked machine-counter bounds; this model is not a timed rate envelope.
shared_assumptions.trusted_source_expiry: Trusted debt and ban expiry constructors denote an internal decision validated for the correct canonical source, current restriction generation and deadline. Peer claims and stale timers cannot construct a trusted expiry. Timer authentication, clock correspondence and the expiry policy are implementation obligations. A trusted debt expiry removes all debt in one transition and a trusted ban expiry removes only the ban. The model has no partial decay, no per-unit refund and no clock, so an implementation with gradual decay must refine each full reset to one trusted debt expiry event.
shared_assumptions.atomic_source_admission: Source eligibility, shared-credit consumption, pending reservation and receipt emission linearize against one pre-state. In the policy/source composition, policy receipt validation and the actual peer identity belong to that same transition. The raw plan and commit helpers are not independently callable runtime admission APIs.
shared_assumptions.source_admission_receipts: AdmissionReceipt values come only from successful internal attempts and preserve the selected pending index and generation through the callback lifecycle. Network input cannot forge or alter them; indices refer to the same fixed pool across a run.
shared_assumptions.bounded_policy_processing: One process-wide policy-work balance gates every modeled attempt and publication before processing. A processed operation spends exactly one credit even when denied. Work capacity and rate and the handshake rate are fixed in module 42. The guard, charge and delegated policy/source event use one serialized pre-state. Already constructed policy receipts are inputs; their creation, pre-guard work, exhausted guards, maintenance and completion need separate cost accounting.
shared_assumptions.bounded_policy_queries: Module 43 constructs policy receipts internally only on the positive-work-credit branch, using the current view and the attempted identity. Authentication and identity inputs must come from verified credentials. The guard, query, charge and policy/source admission use one serialized pre-state. The per-processed-operation cost weight must cover bounded query and receipt production plus delegated work; pre-guard authentication, exhausted guards, maintenance and completion remain outside that weight.
shared_assumptions.finite_ingress_polls: Each modeled poll has finite fuel and a stable finite sequence of ingress events. Runtime dispatch, state updates and saved queue continuations preserve this sequence; external arrivals and queue materialization require separate refinement.
shared_assumptions.bounded_ingress_dispatch: A supplied eventCost bounds all per-dispatched-event work outside the policy-operation and accepted-handshake weights, including exhausted-credit guards, dispatch, maintenance, completion and clock handling. Concrete input, table and queue bounds must justify this weight. Queue creation, authentication before dispatch, empty-poll overhead and executor/waker costs are outside this assumption.
shared_assumptions.persistent_ingress_queue: The runtime atomically retains the queued continuation and its current resource state between polls, and appends each represented finite arrival batch exactly once behind retained events in arrival order. Queue allocation, capacity, overload loss and concurrent producer refinement are separate obligations.
shared_assumptions.unit_ingress_service: Each delivered service round appends its finite arrival batch and dispatches one head event if available, using one unit of poll fuel. The arrivals function names batches by successive round indices. The runtime must deliver enough such rounds; the model does not establish wall-clock latency or fairness for arbitrary poll-fuel schedules.
shared_assumptions.variable_ingress_service: A finite schedule lists delivered turns, each with its own finite fuel and finite arrival batch. Each turn appends its batch once behind retained work and then polls with that fuel against the carried resource state. Zero-fuel turns retain arrivals and state; unused fuel is not banked. Prefix progress requires total delivered fuel equal to the prefix length plus a natural-number slack witness. The runtime must refine these turns and supply enough fuel; elapsed time, fairness, queue capacity and overload are separate obligations.
shared_assumptions.bounded_ingress_admission: The queue-entry limit is fixed and the initial backlog fits it. Admission and enqueue linearize before each poll, preserving the old backlog and accepting only the earliest arrivals that fit the free entries. The remaining suffix is rejected. Runtime refinement must bound payloads and admission costs separately and protect required cleanup, clock and control delivery or justify safe loss and retries.
shared_assumptions.weighted_ingress_payload: One immutable natural-valued charge function applies to every retained ingress event throughout a finite schedule. Entry and payload limits are fixed, and their respective invariants require initially fitting queues. A runtime refinement must establish that charges dominate retained payload storage, cannot be understated by peers, and cover ownership and sharing correctly; fixed entry overhead needs its own dominance bound. Offered batches, rejected suffixes, temporary selections and proof certificates are outside the retained-queue bound.
shared_assumptions.bounded_ingress_scan: A fixed natural admission allowance selects only an offered batch's FIFO prefix before payload and entry admission. Examined rejections are distinct from the caller-owned unexamined suffix. Each selected event receives an independent symbolic scanCost, including zero-payload and rejected events. Runtime refinement must bound or lazily produce offered batches, justify dominating scan charges, separately account for backlog measurement and other omitted work, and define external suffix ownership, resubmission, wakeups and mandatory-event delivery.
shared_assumptions.persistent_ingress_resumption: The caller atomically retains the unexamined FIFO and the admitted queue/resource state across finite delivered turns. Each fresh finite batch is appended exactly once after the deferred FIFO before a fixed scan allowance selects a prefix. Only the unexamined suffix is retried; examined admission rejections leave this FIFO. Deferred storage is unbounded in the model and requires separate runtime ownership, capacity and cost arguments. Enough delivered scan fuel ensures examination of an original deferred prefix, not admission or execution; real wakeups, cancellation, restart and mandatory-event delivery require refinement.
shared_assumptions.bounded_ingress_resumption: The caller atomically carries the returned deferred FIFO and the admitted queue/resource state into each delivered turn. Each fresh finite batch is appended exactly once after the deferred FIFO before a fixed scan allowance selects a prefix. A fixed caller-owned deferred capacity then retains only the earliest unexamined prefix; the remaining suffix is reported to the caller as explicit overflow and is not retried automatically. Examined admission rejections leave the FIFO. The model keeps scan and service allowances, entry and immutable-payload limits, and one carried queue/resource state separate. Runtime ownership, allocation, overflow disposition and resubmission delivery, cancellation, restart and fairness remain refinement obligations.
shared_assumptions.bounded_ingress_handoff_schedules: Finite sequential caller-supplied schedules use a fixed deferred capacity and scan allowance, with per-turn service fuel and fresh arrival batches. Each turn transfers only the capped deferred prefix and admitted queue/resource state; unexamined overflow is returned as chronological output history. The empty-schedule deferred bound requires initial fit. Output histories need not fit the deferred cap. Concrete ownership, overflow delivery/disposal, storage, cancellation, restart, fairness and fuel delivery remain external obligations.
shared_assumptions.bounded_ingress_handoff_service: Service uses a finite sequential schedule with exactly one ingress scan per delivered turn and a fixed deferred capacity. An explicit natural slack witness requires the original prefix, not necessarily the whole deferred input, to fit capacity. Only whole-prefix examination also takes a second slack witness that the delivered turn count covers the prefix length; the partial-prefix equation takes no turn-count premise. Fresh finite arrival batches and dispatch fuel are arbitrary. Examination is separate from successful admission and dispatch. The model does not supply runtime turns, fairness, wall-clock latency, storage or concrete cost bounds.

claims.property: Selecting any held pending slot, or any index at or beyond a finite pool's length, refuses admission without changing the state and emits no admission receipt. claims.property: A policy receipt that is denied in the current view yields no resource transition and no pending receipt. claims.property: Given an allowed current policy receipt, validated source permission, positive shared credit and a free selected lease, admission in either swarm charges the source, spends one credit and reserves exactly that lease for every finite pending prefix and suffix. Prove the runtime accepted-start counter follows successful internal receipt emission without omissions or duplicates.

claims.property: Policy publication applies the existing generation-guarded policy action while preserving the entire source-admission state. claims.property: Accepted starts counted from emitted receipts agree with the state-dependent source-trace erasure. Account separately for rejected-attempt work, policy processing, maintenance, established resources and configuration changes; the theorem is not an honest-admission or wall-clock fairness guarantee.

claims.property: An independent shared policy-work budget gates attempts and publications before the policy/source transition. Refine every attempt and publication path, including denied and stale operations; the input policy receipt is already constructed and its production cost is outside this model.
Bound exhausted-budget guards and define how delayed publications and policy recovery receive service without violating the work cap.

claims.property: Every attempt or publication processed with positive work credit consumes exactly one work credit, including denied attempts, unvalidated sources and stale publications. claims.property: Only trusted ticks refill the independent policy-work bucket at its fixed rate, capped at its capacity. Claimed time is a complete no-op. claims.property: An exhausted policy-ingress attempt preserves the complete modeled state and emits no admission receipt. Extend the coupled state to established resources and live per-source pending attribution.

Relate trusted ticks and poll scheduling to real elapsed time. The result is per finite poll, not a process-wide rate or latency qualification; established resources, restart and cap changes remain open.

Relate trusted ticks and delivered fuel to real time; refine configuration changes and restart persistence separately.

claims.property: A finite bounded handoff schedule reports each turn's unexamined overflow in chronological FIFO order through the returned overflow projection. Overflow is excluded from subsequent internal resubmission. The trace is an output history of unbounded length; this does not prove external delivery, mandatory-event handling, progress or bounded log storage.

claims.property: Composing bounded handoffs preserves admitted entry and immutable-payload bounds under their separate initial-fit premises, the original pending-capacity bound, and the service fuel in the examined-arrival schedule. claims.property: The recursive whole-schedule disposition count equals the length of the initial deferred FIFO followed by all fresh arrival batches. It counts every examined occurrence, every unexamined overflow occurrence and the final deferred FIFO exactly once in that recurrence. Examined candidates include later entry or payload rejections. claims.property: A deferred prefix whose length fits the fixed capacity survives truncation exactly, followed by an explicitly constructed retained suffix. After one ingress scan, a fitting original tail remains ahead of the previous suffix and fresh arrivals. This preserves FIFO occurrences, without requiring the entire offered suffix to fit.

claims.property: For any finite schedule with exactly one ingress scan per turn, the examined trace starts with the first min(turn count, original prefix length) occurrences of a fitting original prefix. A constructed suffix gives an exact append equation. Fresh arrival batches and dispatch fuel are arbitrary, including zero dispatch fuel.

claims.property: A fitting original deferred prefix is fully examined in FIFO order when a finite schedule delivers at least its length in turns with one ingress scan each. claims.property: For any fixed scan allowance, the number of examined occurrences across a bounded handoff schedule is at most the sum of delivered scan allowances. With one scan per turn this is the turn count. Zero scan allowance and an empty schedule examine nothing. These are event-count bounds; they do not bound CPU, allocation, enqueue, overflow handling or wall-clock work.
open_implementation_obligations: Account for concrete per-scan, queue construction, allocation, overflow and scheduler costs outside the occurrence count.
